title: [D2 Context] Flatten-layer views over normalized events
summary: The bottom of the Context Builder's three view layers exists: sql/migrations/0005_flatten_layer.sql creates eight plain views over helena_normalized_events — flows, the DNS/TLS/HTTP layer-observation rows, and the unpacked DNS queries, DNS responses, HTTP requests and HTTP responses — each carrying tenant, sensor, capture sha256, record offset, event id and schema version on every row. Nothing is materialized, and the reason that is safe was measured rather than assumed.
assumption_validated: That a typed flat layer can be built over the stored JSONB without materializing anything and without losing 'absence is not emptiness'. Both halves hold, measured against RisingWave 3.0.3: (a) a materialized view over these plain views is accepted and returns rows, including over `jsonb_array_elements(...) WITH ORDINALITY` and over a `UNION ALL` of two such branches, and `TUMBLE(helena_flatten_flows, flow_start, INTERVAL '5 minutes')` is accepted directly off the plain view and splits the 62-record sample 59/3 across the 21:35:00Z boundary; (b) a set-returning function collapses 'array was empty' and 'layer never observed' into the same zero rows, so the distinction is carried by a per-layer observation row whose existence is the statement of observation and whose count column may read 0. tcp.24 (TLS observed, ALPN empty) and udp.28 (no application layer at all) are the two real records that demonstrate it. One negative result recorded: every HTTP/1 observation in the sample holds as many responses as requests, so no test over real HTTP/1 data can tell request_count from response_count — mutation-checked, the mutation passed until a test built on a shortened real record was added.
makes_buildable: Task 13 (windowed host-context aggregation) has helena_flatten_flows with flow_start as a TIMESTAMPTZ that TUMBLE accepts off the plain view, src_address as the host key, and the four counters still split by direction. Task 14 (entity extraction) has the per-entity source rows it needs: DNS query names, DNS response records with section/type/value and their position in the chain (never an index), TLS SNI and client JA3/JA4, and HTTP+HTTP/2 URIs in one view with a protocol column. Task 17 (view-layering boundary tests) has a machine-parseable declaration block above every object — `Layer:` / `Object:` / `Reads:` / `Read by:` — and eight objects that all read the source, which is the only layer allowed to.

verification.detail: 480 passed in 124 s, whole suite, with the engine started by the conftest fixture (in-memory, nothing left behind). 36 of them are the new tests/test_context.py, all by execution against a throwaway schema on a real engine: the migrations are applied by the real runner, the records are put through the real Normalizer and EventStore, and the views are queried. `make check` (uv lock --check, compileall, the suite) also passes. Four mutation checks were run and each was watched to fail before the file was restored: dropping `WHERE observation ? 'tls'` (3 tests fail), emitting a literal instead of e.event_id in one view (the identity test for that view fails), and making helena_flatten_http.request_count read the response array (passed until the shortened-record test was added, then failed).

deferred: The TLS client offer — cciphers, cexts, csigs, csvers — and the server extension list sexts stay in the JSONB. Nothing above reads them, and a view per unread array is structure ahead of the increment that needs it. The record is whole in helena_normalized_events.observation, so nothing is lost.

The ALPN values. `alpn_count` is on helena_flatten_tls because the observed-but-empty case is real in the sample (tcp.24), but the negotiated protocol strings are not unpacked into rows — nothing above needs them yet.

Splitting a URI into a host part. concept/instruction.md §6 wants the host part in a domain column, and what counts as a domain is a Public Suffix List question (prd task 15); the flatten layer has no domain column at all and stores the URI exactly as supplied, query string included.

The declaration-comment parser and the layering boundary test. The declaration blocks are written in 0005 in a parseable form, but the test that fails when one is missing is prd task 17, and migrations 0001-0004 still carry their declarations as prose rather than in that form — retrofitting them belongs with the test that reads them.
lessons: task 12: RisingWave 3.0.3 supports the whole flatten construction and it survives into a streaming plan — measured, not inferred: `jsonb_array_elements(x) WITH ORDINALITY AS t(value, index)` works in a plain view; a CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW over such a view is accepted, backfills and returns rows; and so is one over a view whose body is a UNION ALL of two such branches. `TUMBLE(<plain view>, <timestamptz column>, INTERVAL '5 minutes')` also works. The lateral alias must be the `AS t(col, ordinality_col)` form — `FROM ev, jsonb_array_elements(...) AS q` then referring to `q.value` fails to bind.

task 12: When the argument to jsonb_array_elements is NULL — the layer key is absent — it yields zero rows rather than raising, so an unpacking view needs no WHERE guard. That is also exactly why absence and emptiness collapse there, and why each layer family needs an observation row of its own.

task 12: `to_timestamp((observation->>'ts')::DOUBLE PRECISION)` round-trips every one of the 62 sample epochs back to the same float exactly (asserted, not spot-checked), so typing the start time as TIMESTAMPTZ in the flatten layer loses nothing.

task 12: psycopg parses the query for placeholders as soon as ANY parameter sequence is passed, so `connection.execute("... LIKE 'helena_flatten_%'", ())` raises ProgrammingError about a malformed placeholder. A test helper that always forwards *args has to pass `args or None`.

task 12: The sample cannot distinguish helena_flatten_http.request_count from response_count on the HTTP/1 branch — all eleven HTTP/1 observations hold as many responses as requests. HTTP/2 does separate them (tcp.0: 1 request, 3 responses). Where real data cannot reach a branch, the technique that worked twice here is a temporary tmp_path capture holding a REAL record changed only in a way the contract permits (a second real record's udp block added; a response list shortened), put through the real normalizer — never a hand-written record and never committed as a fixture.

task 12: The layer-coverage fixture (tests/fixtures/captures/ace6ca33…, 10 records) is the right input for D2 view tests: it holds all six layer combinations including the flow with no application layer and the TLS observation with an empty ALPN, so a view test over it covers what a test over the full 62 records covers, in a tenth of the rows and with per-record assertions that stay readable.
failed_approaches: task 12: Testing helena_flatten_http's two count columns against the summed totals of the whole sample. It passes with request_count reading the response array, because the sample holds 15 HTTP/1 requests and 15 HTTP/1 responses. A sum over a capture is not a test of a per-row column; the per-row comparison against the fixture, plus the shortened-record case, is.
next_session_should_know: The flatten layer is eight PLAIN views in sql/migrations/0005_flatten_layer.sql: helena_flatten_flows, _dns, _dns_queries, _dns_responses, _tls, _http, _http_requests, _http_responses. Read them, do not re-derive columns out of the JSONB — that is the duplication the layer exists to prevent. Every row starts with the same six identity columns (tenant, sensor, capture_sha256, record_offset, event_id, schema_version) in that order; tests/test_context.py::FLATTEN_SHAPES is the second copy of the layer's interface and is asserted against the engine, so adding a column to a view means editing that table too — deliberate friction. Three shape facts to build on rather than rediscover: helena_flatten_flows keeps the counters bidirectional and has no total column on purpose; helena_flatten_http_requests/_responses are HTTP/1 and HTTP/2 in one view with a `protocol` column, where a NULL exchange_number (and a NULL response content_length) is a property of HTTP/2 having no such field, not an unobserved value; and a layer-observation row's EXISTENCE is what says the layer was observed, so 'this flow observed DNS' is a row in helena_flatten_dns and never a flag on the flow. Task 13 should note that TUMBLE works directly off helena_flatten_flows.flow_start and that the sample splits 59/3 across 21:35:00Z. Nothing here is materialized and the signal layer above must not materialize a flatten view either — the measurement that a streaming MV over these views works is in tests/test_context.py::test_a_materialized_view_can_be_built_over_a_flatten_view, which is the evidence the decision rests on. src/helena/context.py is still Python-free and now says why, with maturity 'experimental'; docs/decisions/0015-the-flatten-layer.md carries the rest. Open from earlier sessions and untouched here: bin/README.md's dangling reference to scripts/build-binaries.sh, and the two remaining cross-cutting open questions in concept/08 (the record lost at a catch-up boundary, and durability for the single store).
